title: Launch Window Broker: playbook + capacity-hedge matrix for cross-surface releases
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Create a lightweight Launch Window Broker (process + checklist + small spreadsheet/tooling) that standardizes how runtime, console, and API teams reserve slots, hedge capacity, and communicate fallbacks and escalations for coordinated release trains. The deliverable includes an operator playbook, an annotated capacity-hedge matrix (by region and tier), a notification wiring diagram for the signal mesh, and a small set of templates for cutover messages and rollback triggers.
rationale: We keep encountering last-minute contention between runtime and console deploys during weekly release lanes. The broker will reduce collisions, make capacity commitments explicit, and provide deterministic fallback lanes so customer-impacting rollouts are less likely during peak traffic.
scope:
- Define slot reservation semantics (soft hold, hard hold, surge window)
- Define capacity-hedge levels per environment (staging / canary / prod) and per region
- Create operator playbook and cutover checklist
- Implement notification templates & PagerDuty/Slack wiring examples
- Publish a Confluence playbook and a shared Google Sheet matrix
- Run 2 rehearsal windows with stakeholders
out_of_scope:
- Building full automated broker service (this is a process + lightweight tooling MVP)
- Automatic capacity provisioning changes in infra (SRE will be consulted)
- Changes to billing or quota systems

tasks: PM: Draft reservation semantics doc and sample calendar slots
Eng (runtime): Provide capacity headroom targets for canary/prod
SRE: Validate hedge matrix and blackout windows per region
Console: Define any UX constraints for console-driven deploy signals
Launch Ops: Integrate templates into weekly cadence and test comms
Design: Create simple status badge assets for 'Slot Reserved / Active / Cooling'
decisions: Soft vs hard holds: agreed soft holds default to 48 hours, hard holds require exec approval
Hedge levels: A/B/C mapped to 10% / 25% / 50% headroom respectively for initial MVP
Rehearsal cadence: two rehearsals scheduled in pre-prod; one to include a simulated failover
open_questions: Should Dedicated customers be allowed to reserve hard holds that block Hosted capacity?
Do we need automated enforcement (deny deploy) or human-assisted mediation for slot conflicts?
How should partner-region capacity be handled when cloud provider quotas are short?
notes: Trade-offs: manual broker is faster to ship and aligns ownership; automation reduces human error but increases infra scope
We must avoid adding friction to high-velocity PLG customers — keep public Hosted lanes unobstructed except for major launches
Consider future integration into Console as a 'Launch Scheduler' card if MVP proves valuable
